title: Developer Behind the AI-Built Adobe Clones Says They Are “Not Anywhere Close to Ready
summary: A developer used Claude Opus 5.5 to build open-source replacements for seven Adobe applications, promoted them across Reddit with a projection of roughly 100% parity within a month, then told Hacker News the project was not anywhere close to ready. Its own roadmap puts it at 45% ready for real work and 2,300 to 4,100 agent-hours from full parity. By Steef-Jan Wiggers

title: eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise
summary: Private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates have been compromised, allowing attackers to forge certificates for any site. The keys were revealed due to low entropy, not through a known breach. Browsers blocked them using revocation lists, but other software had to remove the emSign ECC G3 root. Unpatched systems remain exposed to forged certificates, including client auth and mTLS.

title: Netflix Bridges AWS IAM and Internal Identity with Workload Attestation
summary: Netflix has developed a workload attestation mechanism for Apache Spark jobs running on Amazon EMR. The design combines AWS IAM identity with signed claims from Netflix’s control plane before issuing short-lived internal X.509 certificates, allowing managed compute workloads to authenticate to internal services without directly injecting credentials. By Leela Kumili
